newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Malaysia's Renong gets nod to raise rail stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Malaysia's Renong gets nod to raise rail stake.

text.p: Malaysia's Renong Bhd has received government approval to increase its stake in the privatisation of the country's railways to "50 percent plus one share", consortium partner DRB-Hicom group said on Friday.
The extra share would allow Renong to have effective management control of the group getting the privatisation contract of Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB), current operator of the national railroad.
Under the original privatisation agreement with the government, Renong was to get 50 percent, DRB-Hicom Group 30 percent and Bolton Properties 20 percent.
A spokeswoman for the DRB-Hicom group said the firm's stake in the project would be decreased by one share, making its stake in the consortium 30 percent minus one share.
Renong officials could not be immediately contacted for comment.
KTMB was corporatised in 1991 and will be one of the last large government assets to be handed over to the private sector.
Estimates have put KTMB assets at around two billion ringgit ($760 million). These include landbanks in Malaysia and Singapore, estimated to total about 8,000 hectares (19,768 acres).

The one-share increase for Renong follows recent newspaper reports of a struggle between Renong and DRB-Hicom over future plans for the privatised railway. Both companies have denied they were on a collision course.
The consortium has plans to upgrade KTMB's existing networks but Renong and BRB-Hicom have proposed different plans on how this should be done.
Industrial conglomerate DRB-Hicom controls national car maker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton).
Renong is the country's largest infrastructure developer and has built the 900 km (559 mile) North-South Expressway stretching the length of peninsular Malaysia.
